title: Рассказы для детей
author: Лев Толстой
blurb: Four very short stories Tolstoy wrote for children: the three bears, Filipok, a lion and a dog, and a jump from the mast.
note: Written in the 1870s by an author who died in 1910, so it is in the public domain worldwide.
coverCredit: Ivan Shishkin and Konstantin Savitsky, Morning in a Pine Forest, 1889. Tretyakov Gallery, Moscow. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: Каштанка
author: Антон Чехов
blurb: A lost dog is taken in by a circus clown and learns to perform.
note: Published in 1887 and the author died in 1904, so it is in the public domain worldwide.
coverCredit: Dmitry Kardovsky, illustration for Chekhov’s Kashtanka, 1903. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: Муму
author: Иван Тургенев
blurb: A deaf-mute serf in Moscow rescues a puppy and loves it, but his mistress has other plans.
note: Published in 1854 and the author died in 1883, so it is in the public domain worldwide.
coverCredit: Vasily Polenov, A Moscow Courtyard, 1878. Tretyakov Gallery, Moscow. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: Шинель
author: Николай Гоголь
blurb: A poor copying clerk in St. Petersburg saves for a new overcoat, and it changes his life.
note: Published in 1842 and the author died in 1852, so it is in the public domain worldwide.
coverCredit: Pavel Fedotov, The Fresh Cavalier, 1846. Tretyakov Gallery, Moscow. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: Белые ночи
author: Фёдор Достоевский
blurb: A lonely dreamer meets a young woman on four summer nights in St. Petersburg.
note: Published in 1848 and the author died in 1881, so it is in the public domain worldwide.
coverCredit: Vasily Surikov, the Bronze Horseman at night, St. Petersburg, 1870. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: Капитанская дочка
author: Александр Пушкин
blurb: A young officer is sent to a remote fortress and ends up caught between his duty and the Pugachev rebellion.
note: Published in 1836 and the author died in 1837, so it is in the public domain worldwide.
coverCredit: Vasily Perov, Pugachev’s Court, 1875. State Historical Museum, Moscow. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: Герой нашего времени
author: Михаил Лермонтов
blurb: Five linked stories about Pechorin, a bored and charming officer in the Caucasus who hurts the people around him.
note: Published in 1840 and the author died in 1841, so it is in the public domain worldwide.
coverCredit: Mikhail Lermontov, A Skirmish in the Mountains of Dagestan, 1840. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.
